title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files

reading.body:
This incident shows a general-purpose AI coding and agent tool being used as an operational component inside an active ransomware campaign. Cursor Agent, running Claude Sonnet, was not compromised or tricked into producing novel malware in isolation. It was used during live exploitation sessions, meaning the tool's ability to interpret instructions and execute tasks in an environment was applied directly to attacking victim infrastructure. The failure mode is deployment outside the conditions the tool was built for: an agentic AI system with broad capability was used by threat actors as an exploitation assistant, a use case the tool's safeguards did not prevent in practice.

The campaign also shows that AI assistance lowered the operational complexity for the attackers, allowing hands-on exploitation across multiple organizations in a short window. The targeting of ESXi hypervisors is a deliberate choice to maximize disruption, as encrypting virtual machine files while leaving the hypervisor bootable ensures victims receive the ransom demand. A separate cluster of activity used conventional techniques such as SQL Server exploitation, indicating that AI-assisted intrusion was one method among several rather than the exclusive approach.

What is not established is whether Cursor or Anthropic had any technical means at the time to detect or block this specific misuse, and the reporting represents findings from security researchers rather than confirmed legal findings or admissions by any party involved.

reports.title: Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies
Aurora ransomware targets ESXi, abuses Cursor Agent for exploitation

summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team identified a ransomware group called Aurora that has been active since April 2026, targeting organizations worldwide. The group developed a Linux variant of their ransomware capable of attacking ESXi virtual machine environments. Between April and May 2026, Aurora operators used Cursor Agent, an AI tool running Claude Sonnet, to assist with hands-on exploitation across ten target organizations. The ransomware encrypts virtual machine files while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can see ransom demands, and the group operates a data leak site to publish stolen information.

Researchers discovered that Aurora uses a custom tool called esxi_finder.py to scan networks for VMware ESXi hypervisors and vCenter servers. A separate cluster of Aurora activity was also identified, affecting eight organizations across multiple countries including Israel, Germany, Spain, and the United States. This second group used different tactics, including SQL Server exploitation and data exfiltration to self-hosted storage. The report provides technical indicators and command line options used by the ransomware, detailing how attackers systematically compromise and encrypt victim infrastructure.
